subject: Request: Uptime commitment exception + pilot discount for Novus AI
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novus pilot — request for SLO exception + commercial offset

Marissa / Ben —

Quick ask on the Novus AI pilot (attached SOW draft): they are asking for a written uptime commitment for the pilot phase at 99.95% across multi-region traffic. Given the pilot architecture (cross-region data residency plus on-prem evaluation nodes) and the constrained timeline, our infra team estimates we can guarantee 99.8% for the 90-day pilot, not 99.95.

Customer context: Novus is doing a proof-of-value for a LLM retrieval product — low token volumes initially but high availability for inference in two NA regions + one EU region (for compliance). They want the higher uptime to align with their internal vendor policy before procurement signs PO.

Proposed deal terms to make the customer whole while protecting Redwood:
- Accept a temporary pilot SLO of 99.8% (90 days), documented as an exception in the SOW
- Provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-month invoice if we miss the pilot uptime target
- Commit to a technical mitigation playbook (attached) and a rollback/fallback model route to reduce customer impact on detected outages
- If Novus converts to an annual contract within 120 days and achieves >= $200k ARR, provide a tiered usage discount (5% first year) as a commercial offset

I need deal desk / exec authorization to proceed with these non-standard SLO and credit terms. Legal has flagged that Novus will push for a standard uptime clause; we can add a pilot carveout and an explicit clause that full production SLOs will be negotiated at contract signing.

Attachments: Novus_SOW_v2.pdf, pilot-mitigation-plan.docx

Next steps: can you confirm whether we can route this as a provisional exception with executive approval and who should sign off?

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Novus pilot — request for SLO exception + commercial offset

Thanks Olga — good summary. A couple quick clarifying asks before I take this to approval:

1) Confirmed duration: pilot SLO exception limited to exactly 90 days from go-live and documented in SOW with a clear start/end date?
2) Define operational remediation triggers (what constitutes a breach for the pilot) — the mitigation plan attachment helps but we need a line in SOW that describes incident classification and how credits are calculated (e.g., % of monthly invoice per missed hour).
3) Proposed one-time credit: the 10% figure is fine as a starting point; we should cap total credits for the pilot to avoid outsized exposure. Suggest cap = 25% of first-month invoice.
4) Commercial offset: tie conversion discount to a written commitment (signed MSA or PO) so we don't overcommit for an extended trial.

If we get agreement on the 4 bullets above I will prepare a short exec memo and route to Jonas + Ben for signoff. Legal needs to sign the SOW doc before we send to Novus.

-Marissa
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Team —

I reviewed Olga's ask, Marissa's clarifications, and Ben's guardrails. I approve a provisional SLO exception for the Novus 90-day pilot with the following conditions, which must be reflected in the final SOW and signed before go-live:

1) Pilot SLO: 99.8% uptime for 90 days (start/end dates in SOW). This is a one-time, non-precedential exception.
2) Credit terms: one-time onboarding credit = 10% of first-month invoice if we miss the pilot SLO; aggregate credits capped at 25% of first-month invoice. Credits calculated pro-rata by hours missed per standard credit table (reference: Redwood SLO credit table).
3) Operational controls: runbook acceptance call completed and recorded; mitigation plan attached to SOW; automatic fallback routing to reduced-latency model variant when an availability signal is detected.
4) Commercial upgrade path: a written conversion (signed MSA or PO) to qualify for the 5% first-year usage discount, must be executed within 120 days of pilot start.
5) Legal sign-off: Novus Legal must accept the pilot carveout language; we will not provide production-level uptime guarantees in the SOW.

Marissa — please prepare the exec memo and updated SOW (include the attached mitigation doc) and route to Legal + Procurement at Novus for signature. Olga — please run the SRE acceptance call and capture the go/no-go in writing.

Jonas Weber
